title: Client-Server Networks & Resource Sharing
subtitle: AXIS official topic: client-server vs P2P, shared resources, the three sharing rules, monitoring & print services

readingSections.title: Client-Server vs Peer-to-Peer
readingSections.quickSummary: Client-server: dedicated servers serve requesting clients - centralised control. P2P: every machine is both client and server - no central admin.
content: The client-server model separates roles: SERVERS are dedicated machines providing services (files, print, mail, web, DNS, authentication), while CLIENTS request those services. One request-response cycle: client asks, server answers. The model gives centralised administration, consistent security policy, and scalable services - the enterprise standard.

Peer-to-peer (P2P) flattens the roles: every machine acts as BOTH client and server, sharing files and printers directly with each other. No central server means no central administration or security - fine for a handful of home/soho machines, unmanageable at company scale.

The published exam contrast: centralised control/security = client-server; every node both roles, no central admin = P2P. Server types to recognise: file server (storage), print server (queues jobs), mail server (SMTP/POP3/IMAP), web server (HTTP), DNS server (names), authentication server (logins), database server (structured data).

subsections.title: Role vocabulary
subsections.content:
Client = requests services (browser, mail app, your laptop).
Server = provides services (always-on, powerful, centralised).
Same machine CAN play both roles technically - the model is about dedicated service providers.

quickRevision: P2P: every node both roles; no central admin.
Know the server types: file, print, mail, web, DNS, auth, database.
tricks: 'Every node acts as both client and server' -> P2P, verbatim stem.
Server-type matching: names tell the job (file server stores, print server queues, mail server relays).
patterns: 'Which network type has no central administration?' - P2P.
'Dedicated computer providing resources to clients' - server definition.

readingSections.title: Shared Resources & the Three Sharing Rules
readingSections.quickSummary: Shared resources = data/devices reachable over LAN/intranet. Sharing demands: organisational security, compatibility, and mapping.
content: Shared resources (also called network resources) are computer data, information, or hardware devices easily accessible from a remote computer over a LAN or workplace intranet - shared folders, network printers, central databases, shared drives.
Files and printers are shared under either the P2P or the client-server paradigm, and doing it WELL demands three disciplines straight from the syllabus:

1. ORGANISATIONAL SECURITY - unauthorised access to shared resources is a constant threat; security methods (permissions, authentication) must be established to give efficient parameters.
2. COMPATIBILITY - various client-server operating systems can coexist, but the CLIENT needs a compatible OS or application to use the resource, else problems arise.
3. MAPPING - accessing a shared drive/file requires a shared DESTINATION ADDRESS and NAMING CONVENTIONS (mapping a network drive to a letter like Z:).

subsections.title: Mapping in practice
subsections.content:
UNC path: \\server\share\folder (Universal Naming Convention).
Drive mapping: net use Z: \\server\share - the share appears as a local drive.
Permissions layers: share permissions (network view) + NTFS permissions (local filesystem) - most restrictive wins.

quickRevision: Shared resource = data/device reachable over LAN or intranet.
Rule 1 security: permissions/authentication against unauthorised access.
Rule 2 compatibility: client OS/app must match the resource.
Rule 3 mapping: destination address + naming conventions (UNC, drive letters).
tricks: 'Shared destination address and naming conventions' in the stem -> MAPPING, verbatim.
'Constant threat' to shared resources -> unauthorised access, answered by organisational security.
'Client must have a compatible OS/application' -> compatibility rule.
patterns: 'Which guideline is needed to access shared OS hardware drives?' - mapping.
'Which paradigm shares files and printers?' - both P2P and client-server (the syllabus names both).
'Resources accessible from a remote computer over LAN' - shared/network resources.

pyqPatterns.question: Which rule requires a shared destination address and naming conventions?
pyqPatterns.approach: Mapping - compatibility is OS fit; organisational security is access control.

readingSections.companyNote: The three rules are quoted verbatim in the official syllabus - at least one direct question per slot.

readingSections.title: LAN, MAN, WAN & Intranets
readingSections.quickSummary: LAN = one site; MAN = a city; WAN = countries/continents (the Internet). Intranet = private company network using Internet tech; extranet = controlled outsider access.
content: Scale terms: LAN (Local Area Network) - one building/campus, high speed, privately owned. MAN (Metropolitan) - a city-scale network. WAN (Wide Area) - spans countries/continents by leasing links; the Internet is the largest WAN.

An INTRANET is a private organisational network using Internet technologies (TCP/IP, web servers, browsers) - employee-only access. An EXTRANET extends controlled access to trusted outsiders (partners, suppliers). The INTERNET is the public global network.
Shared resources in the syllabus live on LANs and workplace intranets - that phrasing itself is a testable definition.

subsections.title: Identification phrases
subsections.content:
'One building, high speed, privately owned' -> LAN.
'City-wide' -> MAN.
'Country/continent spanning, leased lines' -> WAN.
'Private company network using web technologies' -> intranet.
'Partners get controlled access' -> extranet.

quickRevision: Intranet = private company web world; extranet = intranet + partners.
Shared resources live on LANs and intranets (syllabus wording).
tricks: The Internet is a WAN - but 'the Internet' and 'intranet' spellings get swapped in distractors; intranet = INTERNAL.
Extranet = intranet opened partially OUTSIDE the company.

readingSections.title: Network Monitoring & Print Services
readingSections.quickSummary: Monitoring tracks traffic/usage for faults and intrusions (sniffers, NMS). Print servers queue jobs centrally; sharing follows permissions.
content: NETWORK MONITORING - named explicitly in the AXIS syllabus ('network monitoring, traffic usage') - tracks traffic and usage patterns to catch faults, bottlenecks and intrusions. Tools: packet sniffers/analysers (Wireshark captures packets for inspection), network management systems (SNMP-based dashboards of bandwidth/uptime), and flow analysers.

PRINT SHARING: a print server accepts jobs from clients, queues them, and feeds the printer - centralised driver management, quotas and audit. Clients install the shared printer by pointing at \\printserver\printername.

File-sharing hygiene: least-privilege share permissions, group-based access (not per-user), audit trails on sensitive folders, and regular access reviews - the organisational-security rule in daily practice.

subsections.title: Monitoring vocabulary
subsections.content:
Packet sniffer - captures frames for analysis (Wireshark).
SNMP - devices report status to a management console (UDP 161).
Bandwidth/latency monitoring - utilisation and delay trends.
Intrusion detection - spotting attack patterns in traffic.

quickRevision: Monitoring = traffic/usage observation for faults + intrusions.
Sniffer captures packets; SNMP polls device health.
Print server = central queue, drivers, quotas.
Share permissions: least privilege, group-based, audited.
tricks: 'Traffic usage' in the stem -> monitoring topic - answer with observation tools (sniffer/NMS).
Wireshark = packet ANALYSER (captures), not a blocker - firewall is the blocker.
Print server questions: the QUEUE is the concept - jobs wait their turn centrally.
patterns: 'Which tool captures packets for analysis?' - packet sniffer (Wireshark).
'Centralised print job handling' - print server with a queue.

pyqPatterns.question: 'Network monitoring, traffic usage' themed questions.
pyqPatterns.approach: Match the tool to the job: capture = sniffer, health-poll = SNMP, block = firewall.

readingSections.companyNote: Monitoring appears in the official topic list - expect a tool-purpose match.

formulas.title: Client-Server Role Table

formula.text: Clients ask; dedicated servers answer - centralised control is the model's whole point.

explanation: Server types: file, print, mail, web, DNS, authentication, database.
P2P: every node both roles; no central admin; fine for tiny setups.
Client-server wins on central security, backup, and scalability.
A single machine can technically play both roles - the model is about DEDICATED providers.

example.prompt: Which machine queues everyone's print jobs?

formulas.commonMistake: Calling P2P 'client-server without wires' - it is role-flattening, not a cabling style.

formulas.title: The Three Sharing Rules (verbatim)

formula.text: Organisational security, client compatibility, and mapping with naming conventions - the syllabus trio.

formulas.whenToUse: Every 'share resources in a client-server network' question.
explanation: Organisational security: unauthorised access is the constant threat - permissions/authentication required.
Compatibility: the client needs a compatible OS/application for the resource.
Mapping: shared destination address + naming conventions (UNC \\server\share, drive letters).

example.prompt: Which rule needs a shared destination address and naming conventions?

formulas.memoryTip: Secure it, match it, map it.
formulas.commonMistake: Attributing naming conventions to security - that is mapping's job.

formulas.title: UNC Paths & Drive Mapping

formula.text: Universal Naming Convention addresses the share; mapping binds it to a local drive letter.

explanation: UNC: \\fileserver\projects - works from Run dialog or Explorer.
Map: net use Z: \\fileserver\projects (or right-click -> Map network drive).
Permission layers: share permissions (network) + NTFS (local) - most restrictive wins.
Group-based grants beat per-user grants for administration.

example.prompt: Reach a share as a local drive.
steps: Map the UNC to a letter.

formulas.commonMistake: Forward slashes in UNC paths - Windows shares use backslashes.

formulas.title: Network Scale Ladder

formula.text: Building -> city -> country/continent; intranet = private company network; extranet = intranet + partners.

explanation: LAN: one site, high speed, privately owned.
MAN: metropolitan/city scale.
WAN: wide geography via leased links; the Internet is the biggest.
Intranet: private, employee-only, Internet technologies.
Extranet: controlled access for trusted outsiders.

example.prompt: Partners need limited access to company resources.

formulas.commonMistake: Confusing Internet with intranet - one letter, opposite privacy.

formulas.title: Monitoring Tool Map

formula.text: Capture packets (Wireshark), poll device health (SNMP 161), analyse usage flows.

explanation: Packet sniffer/analyser: captures frames for inspection (Wireshark).
SNMP: devices report to a management console (UDP 161).
Flow analysis: who-talks-to-what usage accounting.
IDS: intrusion patterns in traffic.

example.prompt: Inspect packet contents on the wire.

formulas.commonMistake: Wireshark as a blocker - it observes; firewalls block.

formulas.title: Print Service Logic

formula.text: Central queue orders jobs; the server manages drivers, quotas and audit.

explanation: Jobs spool (wait) in the server queue - first-come or priority.
One driver point of management instead of every PC.
Connect via \\printserver\printer.
Quotas and audit live centrally.

example.prompt: Everyone prints to one device - where do jobs wait?
example.answer: The print queue on the print server

formulas.commonMistake: Jobs waiting 'in the printer' - they wait in the server's spooler.

mcqs.q: In a client-server network, the CLIENT:
exp: Client = the requester; server = the provider.

mcqs.q: Which architecture makes every machine BOTH client and server?
exp: P2P flattens the roles - no central admin either.

mcqs.q: A dedicated machine providing resources to clients is a:
exp: The server definition - always-on, centralised.

mcqs.q: Shared resources are accessible from a remote computer over:
exp: The syllabus definition: data/devices reachable over a LAN or workplace intranet.

mcqs.q: Which sharing rule requires a shared DESTINATION ADDRESS and naming conventions?
exp: Mapping = addressing + naming conventions (UNC paths, drive letters).

mcqs.q: The 'constant threat' to shared resources named in the syllabus is:
exp: Answered by the organisational-security rule: permissions and authentication.

mcqs.q: Which sharing rule says the CLIENT needs a compatible OS or application?
exp: Compatibility - mismatched clients cannot use the resource.

mcqs.q: Files and printers are shared under which paradigms?
exp: The syllabus names BOTH as file/printer sharing paradigms.

mcqs.q: A network limited to one building/campus is a:
exp: LAN = local area - one site, high speed.

mcqs.q: The largest WAN in existence is:
exp: The Internet spans continents - the biggest WAN.

mcqs.q: A PRIVATE company network using Internet technologies is an:
exp: Intranet = internal web world for employees.

mcqs.q: Partners/suppliers get controlled access to company resources via an:
exp: Extranet = intranet extended to trusted outsiders.

mcqs.q: Which machine QUEUES print jobs centrally?
exp: The print server's spooler holds jobs in order.

mcqs.q: Which tool CAPTURES packets for analysis?
exp: Sniffers observe traffic; firewalls block it.

mcqs.q: SNMP (UDP 161) is used for:
exp: Simple Network Management Protocol - device health polling.

mcqs.q: The UNC path format for a Windows share is:
exp: Universal Naming Convention: two backslashes, then server, then share.

mcqs.q: Mapping a network drive means:
opts: Assigning a local drive letter to a share
exp: net use Z: \\server\share - the share behaves like a local disk.

mcqs.q: When share permissions and NTFS permissions conflict, the result is:
exp: Windows combines them by taking the most limiting right.

mcqs.q: Which is a client-server ADVANTAGE over P2P?
exp: One policy point, one backup point, one admin point.

mcqs.q: Which is a P2P DISADVANTAGE?
opts: No central administration or security control
exp: Decentralisation = every user secures their own node.

mcqs.q: A server that relays email is a ___ server; one that resolves names is a ___ server.
exp: Mail server relays (SMTP); DNS server resolves names.

mcqs.q: Which server type stores centralised files?
exp: File server = central storage with permissions.

mcqs.q: Group-based share permissions beat per-user grants because:
opts: Administration scales - change the group once
exp: Organisational-security rule in practice: manageable, consistent rights.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of a shared HARDWARE resource?
exp: The syllabus definition includes hardware devices - printers are the classic.

mcqs.q: Intranet vs Internet: the intranet is:
exp: Intra = inside the organisation.

mcqs.q: Which tool POLLS device health (uptime, interfaces)?
exp: SNMP agents answer management-console polls.

mcqs.q: A city-wide network is a:
exp: Metropolitan Area Network.

mcqs.q: Which paradigm needs NO dedicated server?
exp: P2P machines share directly - no dedicated provider.

mcqs.q: An authentication server's job:
exp: Central identity checks (the AuthN database host).

mcqs.q: Which is the best practice for sensitive share permissions?
exp: Organisational-security rule operationalised.

mcqs.q: A 'screened' shared folder should first be protected by:
exp: Security rule: authentication gates access; permissions scope it.

mcqs.q: Which network type is privately owned and fastest typically?
exp: Short distances = high speeds you own outright.

mcqs.q: The client's OS failing to open a server share illustrates which rule?
exp: Incompatible client OS/application = the compatibility rule's failure case.

mcqs.q: Which server hosts company web pages internally?
exp: Intranet web servers serve internal pages.

mcqs.q: Bandwidth utilisation trends are reviewed in:
exp: Monitoring = traffic/usage observation (syllabus phrase).

mcqs.q: Which is TRUE about a machine in a P2P network?
opts: It shares its own resources directly with peers
exp: Both roles locally - shares and accesses.

mcqs.q: Which document naming convention maps \\fs1\hr to drive H:?
opts: Drive mapping via net use H: \\fs1\hr
exp: Mapping rule in action.

mcqs.q: Which server type would host the company's employee directory?
exp: Directory = structured central data (users/groups).

mcqs.q: Which statement about client and server OS is TRUE per the compatibility rule?
opts: Various client-server operating systems can be deployed, but clients need compatible OS/apps
exp: Mixed estates work - compatibility is the client-side requirement.

mcqs.q: Which monitoring activity spots an attack IN PROGRESS?
exp: IDS-style pattern watching - part of monitoring's remit.

mcqs.q: The syllabus says mapping 'allows you to access any shared OS hardware drive, file, or resource'. The exam-quoted requirements are:
opts: Shared destination address and naming conventions
exp: Mapping = destination addressing + naming conventions - the quoted pair.

mcqs.q: A P2P office grows to 40 machines and chaos ensues. The architectural fix:
opts: Migrate to client-server with central services
exp: Scale breaks P2P governance - centralise file/auth/print services.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the two sharing paradigms is EXACTLY per syllabus?
opts: P2P and the client-server paradigm are the two technologies used to share files and printers
exp: Both paradigms share files/printers - the syllabus names both.

mcqs.q: A share shows data to a user who should not see it. Which rule failed and where?
opts: Organisational security - permission scoping on the share/NTFS
exp: Over-broad rights = the security rule's failure; fix by least-privilege groups.

mcqs.q: Which deployment matches ALL THREE sharing rules at once?
opts: Authenticated group-based share, compatible clients, mapped UNC drive
Open share, any OS, no path
Hidden folder, no path, no rights
exp: Security (auth+groups) + compatibility (standard clients) + mapping (drive letter) - the trio applied.

mcqs.q: A client maps \\fs1\data but gets 'access denied'. The FIRST rule to investigate:
exp: Access denied = identity/rights failure - security rule first; mapping errors give 'not found' instead.

mcqs.q: Which scenario is compatibility (not mapping)?
opts: A Windows 98-era client cannot read a modern SMB3 share
exp: OS/protocol mismatch = compatibility; path errors are mapping.

mcqs.q: An org wants employees on LAN and at home (VPN) to reach the same shares. The resource set is hosted on:
opts: The intranet (reachable via VPN from outside)
exp: Intranet resources + VPN remote access = the standard pattern.

mcqs.q: Which server-type to task pairing is WRONG?
exp: Print servers queue jobs; DNS resolves names - the pairing is wrong, hence the answer.

mcqs.q: A sniffer is placed on the network and sees everything in CLEARTEXT. The architectural lesson:
opts: Encrypt sensitive shared traffic (SMB signing/encryption, HTTPS)
exp: Monitoring exposes plaintext - encryption is the resource-protection lesson.

mcqs.q: Which statement about share vs NTFS permission layers is TRUE?
opts: Effective right = most restrictive of the two layers
exp: Windows intersects them - the tighter limit governs.

mcqs.q: A print server's queue shows one job stuck and everything behind it waiting. The concept demonstrated:
exp: The queue processes sequentially - a stuck job blocks the line.

mcqs.q: Why do enterprises prefer group-based permissions over per-user?
opts: Membership changes propagate rights instantly - no per-resource edits
exp: Join/leave a group; every share follows - the security rule made manageable.

mcqs.q: An intranet web app must be reachable from a partner firm ONLY. The design:
exp: Extranet = controlled external extension of the intranet.

mcqs.q: Which monitoring finding indicates a COMPROMISE rather than a fault?
opts: Odd outbound traffic to unknown hosts at 3am
exp: Anomalous flows = intrusion signal; the rest are faults.

mcqs.q: The syllabus phrase 'efficient parameters' for shared resources refers to:
opts: Security methods (permissions/authentication) established against unauthorised access
exp: Organisational security 'gives efficient parameters' - controls, not display settings.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct UNC for a share called 'Finance' on server FS2?
exp: Backslashes both levels - the only correct UNC form.

mcqs.q: A P2P share is 'hidden' by a dollar suffix (Share$). Security-wise this is:
exp: Hidden-from-browsing is not access control - the security rule still applies.

mcqs.q: Which pairing of network size to example is correct?
opts: MAN-city cable network; WAN-national bank links; LAN-office floor
exp: Geography ladder: office floor, city, nation.

mcqs.q: Which single sentence summarises the official topic?
opts: Shared resources on LANs/intranets demand security, compatibility and mapping under client-server or P2P paradigms
exp: One sentence: resources + paradigms + three rules - the whole official topic.
